text:
dana: Thanks everyone — posting follow-ups from today's All-hands re: security / privacy / compliance. I'll capture short answers and next steps here. Please ping if you need deeper docs.
priya: Quick clarifying Q on SOC2 timeline. We heard "this year" — can we get a target quarter? :thinking_face:

dana: SOC2 Type II target = Q4. We're doing incremental evidence collection now (policy docs + infra logs), pen test planned Aug, auditor kickoff in Sep.

sam: ISO27001 is on a parallel track but later — planning for certification H1 next year. We'll share scope once audit readiness is validated.

leo: For Redwood Private / VPC — is the control plane fully customer-managed (no peering) or is it a managed peering model? Curious about network isolation guarantees.

ana: Short answer: customer-managed control plane inside your VPC for Private deployments. We provide deployment manifests + operator for maintenance. For on-prem air-gapped option, control plane runs on customer infra with no outbound dependencies. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we do peering options and private links.

mike: Audit logs: default retention, export options, and who can view (SRE vs customer)? Also will logs include token-level traces for support debugging?

dana: Default Console retention = 90 days. Enterprise plan: configurable up to 1 year + S3/GCS export. Access is RBAC-gated: only roles with "audit.read" can access raw logs; support gets entitlement-scoped access with customer approval. We log at these levels: request metadata, token/billing attribution, model selection and model latency; we do NOT log full user prompt text unless customer enables opt-in logging.

mike: Nice. Is there a retention config CLI example?

dana: Yup, example below to enable S3 export and 180d retention for your org:
```
redwoodctl org update --org-id=org_123 --audit-retention-days=180 \
  --audit-export=s3://my-bucket/redwood-audit --kms-key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd
```

leo: About KMS — can customers BYOK? HSM-backed keys? Any policy constraints we should be aware of?

dana: Yes, BYOK supported via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure KeyVault integrations. For HSM-backed keys, we support vendor KMS that is HSM-backed (e.g., AWS CloudHSM via KMS). Short constraints: key policy must allow our service principal to use the key for envelope encryption; customers retain key rotation policies. We're working on an HSM-validated workflow (ETA: early next year).

leo: Any quick API/manifest example to wire KMS during Private deploy?

dana: Sample manifest snippet for Private deploy:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: RedwoodDeployment
spec:
  kms:
    provider: aws-kms
    key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd
    allow_service_usage: true
```

priya: For product teams — if we pin a model version and then the runtime auto-fallbacks, will we get alerts about quality/regression? How does rollback work for compliance-sensitive flows?

dana: Rollouts + canaries: Console shows per-route metrics (latency, token cost, quality evals if you attach prompt sets). Automatic fallback is allowed but only to compatible, approved variants (configurable). For compliance flows, set enforced pinning in the policy so no automatic fallback occurs; you'll get a hard reject instead.
